notes: Instance-level rubrics for this task only: the glTF cross-reference translation (parse-time index staging, post-parse back-translation with bounds-check error flow, write-time index emission) spread as hand-written copies across the cgltf implementation headers. Equivalent refactorings are accepted wherever the stated semantic outcome holds: macro-based, static-helper-based, or reshaped reference resolution all count as long as each lifecycle stage's translation ends up in one place, every site sources it from there, and behavior is unchanged. No rubric requires the original pre-injection macro names, signatures, or code shape.

rubrics.criterion: The reference staging performed while JSON is parsed — turning a freshly read object index into the biased pointer value stored in the target field — is performed by exactly one consolidated implementation definition, and every parse function that handles a reference field (meshes, primitives, attributes, morph targets, skins, nodes, scenes, animations, accessors and their sparse views, textures and their alternate sources, images, buffer views, extension compression objects, material mappings, and the document-level scene) obtains it from there, with no hand-inlined biased arithmetic left at any parse site.
rubrics.rationale: This is the parse-life half of the scattered responsibility in this instance; grading must accept any mechanism (macro, static inline helper, or a differently structured staging scheme) as long as exactly one definition carries the translation and no parse site still spells it.

rubrics.criterion: The post-parse resolution that turns a staged biased value back into an element of the array owned by the parsed model is performed by exactly one consolidated definition that also owns the bounds-check failure flow, and every conversion in the fixup pass sources it from there — no per-object-kind hand-written copies of the back-translation or its check remain in the fixup pass.
rubrics.rationale: The fixup pass contains the densest concentration of the injected copies in this case (every object family walked there); resolving them through one definition while preserving the bounds-check error flow is the substance of the repair, and any equivalent single-definition structure (helper returning an error code, macro, macro pair sharing one arithmetic body) satisfies it.

rubrics.criterion: The write-time recovery of a JSON index from an object pointer is performed by exactly one consolidated definition covering both emission shapes (single index property, and per-element arrays such as joint lists, node child lists and scene node lists), and every writer property that emits a reference derives its index from that definition instead of spelling the subtraction at the emission site.
rubrics.rationale: The writers carry the third lifecycle arm of the same concern in this instance; the repair is complete only when both the 28 single-property shapes and the 3 array shapes share one definition, independent of whether that definition is a macro or a function.

rubrics.criterion: The extension-aisle reference sites — draco and meshopt compression targets, the basisu/webp alternate texture sources, and the material variant mappings — are swept into the new consolidated definitions together with the core sites rather than left as the nearest local copy of the arithmetic.
rubrics.rationale: These sites are inside separate per-extension code paths added at different times, so a pass that follows only the obvious shared helpers leaves them behind; they are the part of the sweep most likely to be missed in this specific repository layout.

rubrics.criterion: The shared emission bodies that material texture properties already reuse remain single shared definitions and now source the index translation from the same consolidated definition as all other writers, instead of keeping a second, separate convention for texture references.
rubrics.rationale: This instance leaves two visibly different conventions next to each other in one file; accepting a repair that unifies only one of them re-creates the same divergence the task asks to remove.

rubrics.criterion: Any new machinery that carries the reference translation is placed entirely inside the implementation-only sections of the headers, with no additions or alterations to the public interface area (public functions, types, struct layouts, enums, error codes, or the public cgltf_*_index helper family).
rubrics.rationale: cgltf is a single-header library whose public area is a frozen compile surface; consolidation that leaks into it changes down-stream builds and is not the refactor this task asks for.

rubrics.criterion: The patch does not leave behind single-use intermediate locals whose only purpose was serving the removed inlined arithmetic (per-site staged numeric temporaries or hoisted index temporaries around the former copies) that the consolidation makes unnecessary.
rubrics.rationale: The injected copies carry this scaffolding and it becomes dead the moment the copies are routed through a consolidated definition; leaving it shows the sweep edited lines rather than removed the concern.

rubrics.criterion: The final tree does not retain redundant parallel carriers of the translation: no commented-out or disabled copies of the removed arithmetic, and no second helper or macro retained next to the chosen consolidated definition that duplicates the same translation for the same lifecycle stage.
rubrics.rationale: A repair that adds the new definitions but keeps the old copies (or both a macro and a helper carrying the same stage) leaves the maintenance burden it was asked to remove; this is graded from the final patch and tree state.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not flip the optional-versus-required character of any reference field: references that were accepted when absent (object family pointers like a primitive's material or a texture view) must still be accepted when absent, references that were rejected when absent or out of range (sparse accessor views, buffer views' buffers, skin components, node children, animation sampler and channel components) must still be rejected with the same error code.
rubrics.rationale: Merging two guard flavors into one definition is the natural consolidation here and the most likely place to silently drop the distinction, which would re-enable previously rejected files and change which parse errors downstream users see.

rubrics.criterion: The boundary semantics of the staged-reference scheme survive exactly: the highest in-range index equals the array count minus one, a staged value equal to the count of stored objects plus one or higher is still rejected, and the absent/null reference is still encoded and recognized distinctly from the zeroth object.
rubrics.rationale: The whole instance is built on an off-by-one representation boundary; any repair touching the bias arithmetic is one arithmetic error away from resolving every reference onto a neighboring object, which the tests would only catch on specific fixtures.

rubrics.criterion: The writer does not change its output formatting or values: index properties and per-element arrays (joint lists, child lists, scene node lists) stay in their current shape with identical separators, brackets, indentation and index values, including the reuse of parsed attribute names as labels.
rubrics.rationale: The engine-side consumers compare written text; the array emission shapes are the most fragile part of the serializer and are exactly where a per-element consolidation is likely to introduce separator or bracket drift.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not alter the public helper family that returns object indices for applications (the size-typed index lookups) or their call contract, nor repurpose them as the internal cross-reference mechanism in a way that changes their typed behavior.
rubrics.rationale: This near-miss surface performs related arithmetic in the same files; folding it into the internal pass is the most tempting out-of-scope edit and silently changes public API behavior this task forbids.
